fixer.summary: The engine now logs a creature dropped from an area because it's cut off from the point of origin as rule='GLOSS.area-of-effect#3', page 177. Before, the rule had no clause number. The change is in `_area_targets` in dungdra/spells.py, which also gets the tag `# SRD[GLOSS.area-of-effect#3]`. Two unit tests in tests/unit/test_spells.py now check for the exact clause (`GLOSS.area-of-effect#3`) instead of the bare unit. tests/srd/test_playing_the_game.py:370 still asserts the bare unit and will still pass, because `EventLog.applied` treats a unit as matching any of its clauses. **I couldn't run anything:** Bash was denied in this session, so the unit tests, the ticket's test with `--runxfail`, ruff and `dev-gate` all still need to be run. The edits are small and formatted by hand to match the code around them.

review.summary: The fix is small and does what T-82 asks. At dungdra/spells.py:1140, the log for a creature behind Total Cover from the point of origin now says rule="GLOSS.area-of-effect#3", and the code above it carries the matching # SRD[GLOSS.area-of-effect#3] tag. In the engine, this is the only place that logs the AoE rule, so no other copy of the clause-less rule string is left. The xfail is removed from test_the_exclusion_is_logged_against_the_blocked_lines_clause, and that test now passes: it checks the logged event's rule and page against what the engine actually does. Both changes are allowed: dropping an xfail when its ticket is fixed, and updating the two unit tests that expected the old clause-less rule string. All gates pass. Nothing is hard-coded, the rule stays in the one area mechanism (_area_targets), and nothing is out of scope. A related problem, objects behind Total Cover still being placed in the area, is already ticketed as T-83, so I filed no follow-up.
